name: Plankton
prior: Academic/compositional: Truax GSX at SFU 1986 = 'the first real-time implementation' of granular synthesis, fixed-waveform (sine) and FM grains, Riverrun (1986), grains 10-30 ms at hundreds to thousands per second (VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Truax, sfu.ca/~truax/river.html, sfu.ca/~truax/gran.html); Xenakis Analogique B 1959 tape sine grains (A); Roads' Cloud Generator / tendency masks (A, cited by the idea); SuperCollider GrainSin = 'granular synthesis with sine tones', built-in Hann envelope, 512 overlapping grains by default (VS: docs.supercollider.online/Classes/GrainSin.html); sonicLAB Cosmosf = real-time stochastic scattering of nested meso/micro events, standalone + VST/AU, Saturn 7 (VS: rekkerd.org p=41812, p=141784, synthtopia.com p=38378). Sieves: Ariza's Python sieve in athenaCL, Max/MSP sieve patches, 'no complete implementation widely distributed' (VS: muse.jhu.edu/article/184240) - no instrument found. Mainstream: scale-quantised grains on sampled audio - FRCTL GRN (VST3, major/minor; VS: kvraudio forum p=9269449), GSDSP Quantum Granulator (AUv3/Logic, 30+ scales; VS: apps.apple.com id6741062705), Cherry Audio Adroit Granular (up to 500 grains, scale/chord quantise; VS: store.cherryaudio.com), Quanta 2 (tuning tables; VS: apps.apple.com id6670520767), GrainHeads (iPad, scales; VS: apps.apple.com id6760582834). Sparse scale-random sparkle is the generative-app staple (Eno/Chilvers Bloom 2008, VS: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloom_(software); the Marbles->oscillator idiom, A). Browser: Web Audio granular demos exist, none a sine-grain voice (A). In Myzel: Koerner (sampled grains, scheduler with grainMax, APP 2081/QP), Tropfen (chirps + Regen), Sporenregen (Gestik scatter of the field's notes, APP 4705). Not found: a held touch voice of synthetic sine grains with Poisson density, a scale sieve and finger-height spread.
costNotes: Measured (M: research/bench/grain_osc_cost.js, Node 22): complex-rotation sine + recursive Hann per grain = 3.8 ns per grain-sample: 5 concurrent grains 19 ns = 0.17 units, 12 = 0.37, 24 = 0.76, 64 = 2.0 (0.581 % core = 1 unit, R: webaudio.md section 4). Default rho x korn = 35/s x 0.14 s = 4.9 concurrent (x1.5 at full velocity ~ 7) + node 0.06 + 3 k-rate params 0.09 + Poisson/random walks per block ~0.02 -> ~0.4 at L1. The cost is parameter-dependent by x5: dichte 200/s x korn 0.5 s = 100 concurrent, capped by 24 slots = 0.9 units, L3 64 slots = 2.2; the app budgets one fixed VCOST per engine (APP 2081-2082), so either cap slots at 12 (L1, <= 0.5 worst, steal the oldest grain) / 32 (L3, <= 1.2) or compute the engine's cost from P (dichte x korn) in playNote. Worklet is right: a native grain = OscillatorNode + Gain (0.06 units while alive) plus ~70 node creations/s per voice through the Koerner scheduler pattern - workable only as a fallback at <= 15 grains/s. Contract (R: section 10) fits: one k-rate detune applied to all live grains per block, freq glide = centre glide, envelopes native on v.out.gain.
soundHeld: At y = 0 (sigma 0) every grain sits on f: the Poisson sum of phase-random Hann sines is a sine with +-3-6 dB random tremolo at the grain rate (A, random-phasor sum) - a 'shimmering Tiefe', soft but alive, the only engine with that texture. At y 0.3-0.5 (sigma 0.45-0.75 oct, sieve on) grains land on the scale degrees within about an octave, Gaussian-weighted around the played note: a sparkling cloud of the mode whose densest point is the note - pentatonic and modal fields sound like a wind-chime chord, a chromatic/12-note field becomes a cluster (the sieve must use the field's scale, APP N.notes 2056, and fall back to semitones only for N.free as the idea says). At y = 1 (sigma 1.5 oct) the cloud has no pitch identity - fine for textures, wrong for melody. Grain pitches are fixed at birth, so a glide leaves a comet tail (correct, distinctive); Bebung via the block detune moves old and new grains together (fine). The 15-40 s tendency walks are inaudible on a 2-s note; they only matter for drones and could be replaced by Ladung. Overlap risk: Sporenregen and Tropfen already rain field notes; Plankton must stay 'sieved sine dust' - no chirps, no transients, no rhythm - or it reads as a third rain.
soundBurst: A hit = rho x 3 for the gate (105/s): a 160-ms gate gives ~17 grains plus a 1.4 x korn tail = a 0.35-s soft splash of scale notes around the lane's note, velocity = density. Distinct (nothing in Myzel is a soft sparkle), but weak as percussion: 140-ms Hann grains have no transient, the hit's pitch is a cloud when the lane's Hoehe is high, and at 1/16 120 bpm (112 ms, APP 5980) 105/s x 140-ms grains smear across the next step. Fix: burst korn = min(korn, gate/2), one short leading grain (15 ms) exactly on f for the transient, burst sigma capped at 0.5 oct.
failureModes: Cost scales x5 with dichte x korn (M: 24 full slots = 0.9 units, 64 = 2.2) while the app budgets a fixed cost per engine - cap slots (12 at L1, 32 at L3) or derive cost from the parameters
Low density (4-10/s) is the Bloom/Marbles generative-arpeggio cliche, not a voice; keep the default dense (>= 25/s) and the grains short enough to read as texture
Chromatic or 12-note fields turn the sieve into a cluster; weight the sieve by scale degree (root/fifth heavier) or limit sigma for dense scales
No transient: Puls hits are soft splashes that smear across fast steps - burst grains must shorten with the gate and a leading 15-ms grain must carry the attack
Pitch identity vanishes above sigma ~0.75 oct; the Gestik Hoehe offset can push a melodic line into a cloud - clamp sigma for the first 300 ms of a note
Phase-random grains on one frequency beat into +-6 dB tremolo at unison; if that reads as 'broken', align grain phase to the running note phase at y < 0.1
Third 'rain' in the app (Tropfen, Sporenregen): the catalogue text must sell the held cloud, not the splash
verdict: Rare: synthetic sine-grain clouds are Truax's 1986 GSX and SuperCollider's GrainSin, stochastic event scattering is Cosmosf, and scale-quantised grains ship in GRN, Quantum Granulator, Adroit and Quanta 2 - all sample-based or compositional, none a held touch voice with a scale sieve under the finger; the nearest familiar sound is the generative-app sparkle (Bloom), which Plankton must avoid at low density. Worklet-feasible and cheap at the defaults (~0.4 units; 3.8 ns per grain-sample measured), but the cost scales x5 with dichte x korn, so slots must be capped (12 at L1, 32 at L3) or the cost computed from the parameters. Held notes are distinctive (a shimmering sine at unison, a sieved cloud of the mode when raised); the Puls hit is a soft splash that needs a short leading grain and gate-shortened grains to survive fast patterns.
